definitions.explanation: A large, impressive house or residence, typically belonging to a wealthy or high-status family. The お prefix adds a sense of respect or refinement.

examples.japanese: {丘|おか}の{上|うえ}にお{屋敷|やしき}が{見|み}える。
examples.english: You can see a mansion on the hill.

examples.japanese: あのお{屋敷|やしき}には{広|ひろ}い{庭園|ていえん}がある。
examples.english: That mansion has a spacious garden.

examples.japanese: {江戸時代|えどじだい}の{武家|ぶけ}のお{屋敷|やしき}が{今|いま}でも{観光地|かんこうち}として{残|のこ}っている。
examples.english: Some samurai mansions from the Edo period still remain as tourist sites today.

notes:
The polite prefix お adds refinement and is standard when referring to mansions or grand residences. Without the prefix, {屋敷|やしき} alone can refer to any large dwelling but sounds more neutral or historical. In modern usage, お{屋敷|やしき} often evokes old money, traditional architecture, or historical estates.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- お{屋敷|やしき}{街|まち} — upscale residential neighborhood
- お{屋敷|やしき}{町|まち} — mansion district (historical)
- {古|ふる}いお{屋敷|やしき} — old mansion
- {立派|りっぱ}なお{屋敷|やしき} — splendid mansion

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {屋敷|やしき} — mansion, estate (without polite prefix)
- {邸宅|ていたく} — residence, mansion (formal, written style)
- {豪邸|ごうてい} — grand mansion (emphasizes luxury and size)
